findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex for same key now races and duplicates work
findings.body: BuildIndex is no longer serialized; the lock is only taken around the cache write. getOrCreateIndex calls GetIndex and then build, so two concurrent requests or watch events for the same key can both see nil and build the index at the same time. Both writes go to the same on-disk dir (bleve.New fails if it exists) or produce duplicate in-memory indexes. The last writer wins, so the other index leaks, and its IndexTenants and IndexedKinds metrics are double-counted. A per-key lock or singleflight is needed.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu. Now that builds run concurrently and write the map under the lock, this read is a data race. A concurrent map write during iteration can crash the process. It should hold RLock.

findings.title: Shared err and counter written from multiple goroutines
findings.body: Inside group.Go, the closures assign to the outer `err` variable and increment `totalBatchesIndexed` concurrently, which is a data race. Since this PR is meant to raise build concurrency, the race is more likely to occur. Use a local `err :=` in the closure and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Init errors are now fatal at construction and Stop no longer gates requests
findings.body: Init now runs in NewResourceServer, and the Init checks were removed from every handler. As a result, Stop setting initErr ("service is stopping") no longer prevents requests from being served after shutdown. Building all indexes synchronously in the constructor also blocks startup. On error, the context created with WithCancel is never cancelled, so it leaks.
